clue.text: Walpole nominated as poet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the given name of Walpole, the eighteenth-century writer and son of the prime minister
second meaning: the Roman lyric poet of the Odes

explanation.surface: A man called Walpole has been put forward as a candidate for the post of poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominated' here means 'named': the forename that Horace Walpole, author of The Castle of Otranto, was given.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin lyric writer Quintus Horatius Flaccus is known in English by this single name, shared with the Gothic novelist Walpole.

clue.text: Reform due in order to set up concert hall

indicators.note: the reworked letters are placed inside the abbreviation for the honour
to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three letters of due, rearranged
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A plan to reorganise dues payments properly so a new concert hall can be built.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit; the shuffled letters sit between its O and M.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome an odeum was a roofed building for musical performances and recitals.

clue.text: Joiner appears before lunch, by George!

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the morning, the time before lunch
per is Latin for by, as in per post
George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a carpenter turns up before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By George!' sounds like an oath, but it splits into by and George, the novelist George Sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The & sign links words together, as in Marks & Spencer, so it is literally something that joins.

clue.text: Failing by a point to pass

parts.note: E, east, is one of the compass points
a lapse is a slip or failing

explanation.surface: Someone fails an exam by a single mark, just missing a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' only places the two pieces side by side; the compass point comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or goes by, so the verb matches 'pass' in the sense of time slipping away.

clue.text: A raw quarter-back who tackled the Trojans

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the hero himself

parts.note: taken as written
a raw day has a chill in the air

indicators.note: going back means the compass quarter is read from right to left

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: An inexperienced American football quarterback who took on a team called the Trojans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter-back' looks like the American football position; split it into a compass quarter and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek warrior fought and killed Hector and many other defenders of Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Is this the attraction of Polar bears?

definitions.text: Is this the attraction of Polar bears?

parts.note: surface reading: what draws people to the polar bears at the zoo
setter's reading: 'Polar' points to magnetic poles, and bears are beasts, so a beast's magnetic pull

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes polar bears so popular with visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Polar' look like part of the bears' name; read it instead as the poles of a magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means personal charisma or physical allure, and literally joins a creature with the force between magnetic poles.

clue.text: Guide for worker going to work

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand
a book is a written work

explanation.surface: Advice for an employee heading off to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' reads as a workplace, but it is a written work.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook is a manual or reference volume that guides its reader through a subject or procedure.

clue.text: You need the right numbers for this children's game

definitions.text: You need the right numbers for this children's game

parts.note: surface reading: a team game that needs the correct number of players
setter's reading: a game in which you win by having the numbers that are called out

explanation.surface: A game for children that can only be played with enough players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right numbers' suggests enough players; in this game it means holding the numbers that are drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a nursery game like bingo, where players cover numbered squares on cards as numbers are drawn.

clue.text: Cut out of the middle of Hereford

definitions.text: Cut out of the middle of Hereford

parts.words: Cut out of the middle of Hereford
parts.note: surface reading: something removed from the centre of the English city
setter's reading: a Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, and a cut is a piece of meat from between its ribs

explanation.surface: Something excised from the centre of the cathedral city of Hereford.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is a city, but also a breed of beef cattle; 'cut' is a cut of meat, not a removal.
explanation.definitionFit: The French name means between the ribs, describing a steak taken from the central rib section of a beef carcass.

clue.text: Revolutionary time not apt for trial

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political uprising is badly timed for a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary time' reads like an era of uprising; 'Revolutionary' is only the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial in the moral sense is a test of resolve, and being tempted is exactly such a testing ordeal.

clue.text: Computer for better transport

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the totalisator, the machine that works out odds and payouts for people who bet
second meaning: to carry or lug something

explanation.surface: A call for a better computer to run the transport system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is not 'improved' but one who bets; the tote is the betting machine at racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote is short for totalisator, a pool-betting calculator, and to tote a bag is to carry it about.

clue.text: Refreshment for the gallery

parts.note: surface reading: snacks sold to the audience in the cheap upper seats of a theatre
setter's reading: the gallery is nicknamed the gods, and this is the food of the gods in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Interval snacks being sold to the people in the theatre gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The highest theatre gallery is called 'the gods', so the clue wants the legendary food of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the Olympian deities ate this substance, which conferred immortality, so it is their refreshment.

clue.text: Dutch settler carries little weight at the Bar

indicators.note: something that carries another thing holds it within itself

parts.note: a Boer is a South African settler of Dutch descent
oz, ounce, is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A slim Dutch colonist at the Bar, as if practising law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bar' looks like the legal profession; here it is a pub, and a boozer is British slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a boozer is a pub, a place with a bar where drinks are served.

clue.text: Hollow pamper'd Jades of - (2 Hen. IV)

definitions.text: Hollow pamper'd Jades of - (2 Hen. IV)

parts.note: surface reading: an incomplete line of verse with a gap to fill
setter's reading: the line is Pistol's in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2, ending with a continent

explanation.walkthrough: Pistol misquotes Marlowe's Tamburlaine, whose horses are the pampered jades of the East; the missing word is the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation from Henry IV Part Two reads 'hollow pamper'd jades of Asia', so the continent completes the line.

clue.text: Powerboat with funnels?

parts.note: surface reading: a fast motorboat
setter's reading: a vessel powered by steam, so it has smokestacks

explanation.surface: Asking whether a racing powerboat would have chimneys.
explanation.walkthrough: A powerboat is normally a speedboat; read it as any boat driven by an engine, here a steam one.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam engines typically has tall funnels for smoke, unlike a modern motor speedboat.

clue.text: Satellite winged for an Apollo mission

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's natural satellite
a bird that is winged has been shot

explanation.surface: A satellite with wings designed for a NASA Apollo flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winged' suggests having wings; it means wounded by a bullet in the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apollo programme's flights were launches aimed at the lunar surface, which is what the compound means.

clue.text: Greyish plant on the lawn

parts.note: sage is a herb
a green is a grassy lawn, as in a village green

explanation.surface: A greyish plant growing on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This colour is the soft grey-green of the herb's leaves, so it is a greyish shade.

clue.text: Wrong river for this reptile

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: A reptile in the wrong river, as if a turtle had lost its way.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is the legal term for a civil wrong; the Oise is a tributary of the Seine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-moving shelled land animal is a familiar example of a reptile.

clue.text: Master desire to be impetuous

parts.note: a headmaster is the head of a school
to long is to desire

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster wanting to act on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire' is a verb here, matching long as in long for.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing ahead without thought is rash and hasty, so a headlong decision is an impetuous one.

clue.text: Female not quite county

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Gwent was a county in south-east Wales

explanation.surface: A woman who doesn't quite fit in with the county set.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwent, a former Welsh county, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, Welsh in origin, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Rustic skill producing capital port

parts.note: a hob is an old word for a country yokel or clown
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A country craft that makes something worthy of a capital port.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob is an archaic word for a rustic, a country bumpkin.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of the Australian state of Tasmania and a harbour on the Derwent estuary.

clue.text: Reckoning say the value of Richard's kingdom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a total or sum
second meaning: Richard III offers his kingdom for a horse, so read as two words it is what the kingdom is worth

explanation.surface: An estimate of what a king's realm is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Richard III cries 'my kingdom for a horse!'; a horse, say, is a mount, so the answer splits as A MOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckoning is a calculated sum or total, and that is what an amount is.

clue.text: No good having female in group

indicators.note: the letter for female goes inside the word for group

parts.note: a unit is a group, as in a military unit
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: It's no good having a woman in the team, a dated complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsuitable or not in condition for its purpose is useless, which is what 'no good' means.

clue.text: Spin out elegant composition above love

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Drawing out a graceful piece of writing that is about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter for love joins the letters of elegant before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out a story is to make it longer, and lengthening something is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Realism is the beauty of Keats

definitions.meaning: first meaning: faithfulness to how things really are
second meaning: what Keats equates with beauty at the close of his Ode on a Grecian Urn

explanation.surface: A critic claims that Keats's poetry is beautiful because it is true to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's Ode on a Grecian Urn ends 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty', so for Keats beauty is this very word; the grid's T, U and H crossings confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism and fidelity to fact are close synonyms, and Keats's famous line makes the two words interchangeable.

clue.text: Kitchener would have held one to be most important

indicators.note: the answer would once have held this letter, so it is the longer word with that letter now gone

parts.note: chief means most important, as in the chief reason
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Lord Kitchener, the field marshal, thought one particular man was supreme.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener looks like the famous field marshal; it is someone who works in a kitchen. Put the numeral back and the cook becomes the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchener is literally a person working in a kitchen, and the cook who runs it is the obvious example.

clue.text: Relating to the order in which flags should be placed

definitions.text: Relating to the order in which flags should be placed

parts.words: the order in which flags should be placed
parts.note: surface reading: the protocol for arranging flags in a display
setter's reading: an order is a botanical grouping, and flags are wild irises, so the plant family that includes them

explanation.surface: Something to do with the correct sequence for hanging national flags.
explanation.walkthrough: A flag is also a name for the iris plant, and 'order' is a rank in plant classification.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the iris family Iridaceae, the botanical group to which yellow flag irises belong.

clue.text: He got MP confused with a witty remark

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled up, so they need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, joining the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A man got a politician muddled with a clever quip.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'witty remark' belongs to the letters being rearranged, not to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothegm is a terse, pointed saying or maxim, a pithy and often clever remark.

clue.text: Divisions housed initially under canvas

indicators.note: being under canvas means sheltering inside a tent, so the letter goes within

parts.note: tents are made of canvas, and to be under canvas is to be camping

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the first letter of housed

explanation.surface: Army divisions billeted in tents in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' is the camping idiom for staying in tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenths are the parts you get when something is divided into ten equal pieces, so they are divisions.
